name: NJ-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+15 district with no Republican on the ballot; independents are the only opposition
Menendez holds a dominant money position: $1.96M raised plus $912K in outside support, while challengers report no fundraising
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 95%
No public polls or expert ratings; the outlook rests on district lean and incumbency
model.rationale: The seat's fifteen-point Democratic lean, Menendez's large financial edge, and the absence of a major-party challenger make an upset highly improbable, and prediction markets corroborate at about ninety-five percent.
model.watch: A late-breaking scandal, consolidated independent challengers, or a surge of outside spending against Menendez could narrow the margin, though a flip remains a long shot.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Aristotle Eliopoulos is an independent standing in for the Republican side.

overview:
New Jersey's 8th District, anchored in Hudson County, leans Democratic by fifteen points. Rob Menendez, seeking another term, enters the general election with roughly two million dollars raised and outside support approaching one million dollars. No Republican filed to run; he faces independents Aristotle Eliopoulos, Craig Honts, and Da'Shone Hughey, none of whom report meaningful campaign finances.

Prediction markets put Democratic chances near ninety-five percent, and the district's fundamentals point the same way. The open questions are turnout and whether any independent can consolidate anti-Menendez sentiment; the family name remains a talking point, but no polling, expert ratings, or major outside spending signals a competitive race. All available evidence points to a comfortable Democratic hold.
